intro: Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature that harms a person's dignity, and everyone has the right to feel safe and respected.
points: Harassment is judged by its effect, not intent — "only a joke" or "just banter" is never a defence.
It can be verbal, non-verbal, physical or online, and a single serious incident is enough to count.
You can be harassed by clients, relatives or visitors — this third-party harassment is not something you must tolerate.
Where someone using services is affected and may be an adult at risk, follow your safeguarding procedures too.
If someone tells you, listen calmly, believe them, and don't promise secrecy you cannot keep; report through the right routes.
Under the Equality Act 2010, the law also protects you from victimisation for raising or supporting a genuine complaint.
